Advances: specled.verification

Surfaced by the orchestrator while grading specled_-ymn (epic specled_-233, 2026-07-26). NOT a defect in that ticket — it did not introduce the pattern, and the pattern is explicitly permitted by the ADR today. This ticket questions whether the permission is well-founded.

## The tension

`specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names` (now superseded by `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach`) reasons as follows: `System.unique_integer/1` is unique only within one BEAM VM; specled runs NESTED (a `mix spec.check` merged run executes the host project's tests, which may themselves exercise specled) and in PARALLEL; all those VMs share `System.tmp_dir!()`; so two VMs can generate the same name and the loser's `File.rm`/`File.rm_rf!` cleanup deletes the winner's in-flight file.

It then carves out: "test-only usages remain fine."

That carve-out does not obviously follow from its own premise. Test setups in this repo overwhelmingly use exactly the pattern the ADR warns about — a `System.tmp_dir!()` root named with a VM-local counter, torn down with `File.rm_rf!`:

    root = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "specled_hashstore_#{:erlang.unique_integer([:positive])}")
    File.mkdir_p!(Path.join(root, ".spec"))
    on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf!(root) end)

Measured 2026-07-26: 30 test files combine `System.tmp_dir!()` with `unique_integer`. `:erlang.unique_integer([:positive])` restarts low in each fresh VM and increments, so two concurrently-started VMs are LIKELY to mint overlapping values rather than unlikely. On collision the failure is the exact one the ADR describes, with the blast radius pointed at a test rather than a subject: VM B's `on_exit` `File.rm_rf!(root)` deletes VM A's in-flight fixture tree mid-test.

## Why it matters more than it looks

specled's own gate is the nesting mechanism. `mix spec.check` executes tagged tests, and this project dogfoods itself, so a specled test suite can be running inside a specled run. That is not hypothetical for this repo specifically.

Concretely observed shape (not a live failure, an inspection): `test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs` is `async: true`, mints its root with `:erlang.unique_integer`, and asserts `refute Enum.any?(tmp_siblings(path))` over `File.ls!` of that root's `.spec/` directory. If two VMs collided on the root, one run could observe the other's temp sibling and fail an assertion that is otherwise sound — a flake that would read as a real cross-VM-uniqueness regression, which is the most expensive kind of false signal in exactly this area.

## What to decide

Not obviously "convert all 30 files". Options, in rough order of value:

1. Narrow the carve-out's WORDING to what is actually safe, and say why. If the reasoning is "a colliding test root is tolerable because the window is small and a flake is cheap", state that as the accepted risk. An unexplained blanket "test-only usages remain fine" invites a reader to conclude the nesting hazard stops at the lib/ boundary, which is not true.
2. Convert only the tmp roots whose tests ASSERT on directory contents (`File.ls!` + `refute any`), since those are the ones where a collision produces a false failure rather than merely a deleted scratch dir. `hash_store_test.exs` is the known member of that set; sweep for others.
3. Provide a test helper (`SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` is already public and available to tests) and adopt it in new tests, leaving existing ones alone.

Do NOT bulk-rewrite 30 files without deciding 1 first — the ADR text is the actual deliverable here, and a mass edit would drag ~30 test files' owning subjects into branch-guard's impacted set for no semantic gain (see specled_-chb for how expensive that coupling gets).

MEASURED EVIDENCE, from an independent test-quality review of specled_-ymn (2026-07-26). Corroborates this ticket's premise with numbers rather than reasoning.

`:erlang.unique_integer([:positive])` sampled across three FRESH VMs, three draws each:
  VM 1: 1346, 1378, 1410
  VM 2: 1348, 1380, 1412
  VM 3: 1348, 1380, 1412

Two of the three VMs produced byte-identical sequences. The value space is small and heavily overlapping across VMs, so a cross-VM collision on a test root named `specled_hashstore_<counter>` is plausible rather than theoretical — which is the point this ticket questions in the ADR's carve-out.

Mitigating nuance for prioritisation: in a FULL-suite run the counter is also consumed by unrelated work in seed-randomised module order, so exact collision is considerably less likely than the isolated probe above suggests. The hazard is real but not high-frequency.

Concrete added detail on the blast radius in test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs: on collision, `File.ls!` in the tmp_siblings/1 helper RAISES where the older `File.exists?` could not, if the other VM's on_exit `File.rm_rf!(root)` lands first — so a collision now surfaces as an exception rather than a quiet false assertion. Note the same collision already breaks that file's many pre-existing `File.read!` / `File.regular?` assertions, so this is a widened blast radius on a pre-existing hazard, not a new one.

Also in scope for option 2 of this ticket: test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs operates on the genuinely shared `_build/<env>/.spec` directory (async: false). Its `after` block deletes every `xref_mfa.etf.tmp.*` in that shared directory, which would include a concurrently compiling VM's in-flight sibling. Its new `assert Enum.any?` direction is the SAFE one (foreign siblings are additive noise that cannot break it), but the cleanup sweep is not.

Suggested minimal fix, pleasingly on-theme: change the root to `"specled_hashstore_#{SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix()}"`. That removes the root collision entirely and makes every refute in that file cross-VM-safe by construction — using the very helper this epic's specled_-ymn work exists to promote.

ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: small
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
All three options are open. Recommended minimum = option 1 + the two option-2 sites.

OPTION 1 (the actual deliverable — do this first, it is what the ticket asks to "decide"):
Edit `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach.md`, replacing the bare sentence at line 48 ("Test-only usages remain fine.") with wording that either (a) states the accepted risk explicitly, or (b) narrows the permission. Concrete end state — the Decision section must say, in substance:
  - `System.unique_integer/1`-named roots under `System.tmp_dir!()` in `test/` are ACCEPTED RISK, not safe-by-construction: the nesting hazard is identical to lib/'s (a `mix spec.check` merged run executes tests inside a specled run), but the blast radius is a flaked test rather than a corrupted subject artifact, and blanket conversion of 30 files would drag their owning subjects into branch-guard's impacted set for no semantic gain.
  - The permission does NOT extend to tests that ASSERT on directory contents (`File.ls!` over a shared or tmp root, or a cleanup sweep that deletes by glob in a shared dir). Those shall use `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0`, because there a collision produces a false failure/raise rather than a deleted scratch dir.
  - New tests allocating shared-tmp roots should reach for `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0`.
Do NOT edit the `affects:` list (see risk notes). Leave the superseded ADR `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names.md` untouched.

OPTION 2a — `test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs:10`: change
  Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "specled_hashstore_#{:erlang.unique_integer([:positive])}")
to
  Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "specled_hashstore_#{SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix()}")
This makes the `File.ls!` in `tmp_siblings/1` (:20-24) and both `refute Enum.any?` at :274 and :413 cross-VM-safe by construction, and removes the raise-on-collision path the comment flags.

OPTION 2b — `test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs`: the root is the genuinely shared `_build/<env>/.spec` (`@manifest_path`, :14) and cannot be uniquified. Narrow the destructive `after` sweep at :412-420 so it deletes only siblings this VM created — filter on `String.starts_with?(&1, "xref_mfa.etf.tmp.#{System.pid()}_")` instead of the bare `"xref_mfa.etf.tmp."` prefix (the pid prefix is already asserted at :409-411, so the filter is available). Optionally apply the same pid-scoping to the `litter` filter at :381-387 so `assert litter == []` cannot be broken by a concurrently compiling VM's in-flight sibling.

OPTION 3 (optional, cheap): note in the ADR Consequences that `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` is public and available to tests (already precedented at `test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_bootstrap_test.exs:20`). Explicitly do NOT convert the other ~28 files.

Sweep already done for you: the only other `File.ls!`-over-tmp-root candidates are `test/specled_ex/coverage/mfa_lines_test.exs` (:39 already uses `:crypto.strong_rand_bytes` for the root — SAFE, no change) and `test/test_support/evidence_helpers.ex` (:87/:98 `File.ls!` is over a repo-local git objects dir, not the tmp roots at :31-32 — no change needed). No further discovery required.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
.spec/decisions/specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach.md, test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs, test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs

== RISK NOTES ==
REALIZATION HASHES: no impact. `.spec/realization_hashes.json` has exactly one top-level key, `"api_boundary"`, and contains no test-file or hash_store/tracer test entries (`grep -n "hash_store_test\|tracer_test" .spec/realization_hashes.json` => empty). All three edits are ADR prose + test bodies; no `lib/` function body changes, so the realization-drift gate is untouched.

BRANCH GUARD — favourable, but only if you don't widen affects:
- Editing the ADR sets `analysis.decision_changed? = true` (lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex:100-101), which HELPS the whole 22-ticket PR satisfy `branch_guard_missing_decision_update`.
- Do NOT add entries to the reach ADR's `affects:` list (lines 5-13). `specled.append_only.adr_affects_widened` (lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:2) fires on widening an existing ADR's affects. Prose-only edits inside Context/Decision/Consequences are not append-only-checked.
- The two test edits are honestly co-changed by the ADR edit: `test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs` is on `specled.binding`'s surface (binding.spec.md:26) and `specled.binding` already lists `specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach` (binding.spec.md:41); `test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs` sits under `specled.compiler_tracer`, which also already lists it (compiler_tracer.spec.md:45). So no false spec-graph assertion is needed here — this ticket does NOT hit the prose_guard wall that forced the specled_-chb revert.
- hash_store_test.exs carries `@moduletag spec: ["specled.binding.hash_store_atomic"]` (:4), so `branch_guard.file_touch_tagged_tests_attested` applies and file-touch yields — low risk of a spurious subject-update finding.

CONFLICT DETAIL:
- specled_-asb edits `test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs:241-293` (merge_edges property). This ticket edits :375-420 of the same file. Different regions, but same-file — sequence them or expect a trivial merge.
- specled_-chb edits `lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex` temp-name narration and may strengthen `specled.verify.command_output_capture_dir` in verification.spec.md; both chb and ehv Advance `specled.verification` and both are downstream of the SAME ADR's narrative. If chb also revises `cross_vm_temp_names_reach`, that is a direct file conflict. Ordering suggestion: land ehv's ADR wording first so chb's one-line pointers point at complete text.
- specled_-26g fixes shared-$TMPDIR pollution in `test/specled_ex/coverage/store_test.exs` — different file, but it is exactly the class this ticket's ADR wording governs. Land ehv option 1 first so 26g knows whether to use `cross_vm_suffix/0`. Note td7 already modified store_test.exs (+38 lines), so 26g has its own merge surface there.

NO HARD DEPENDENCY on any other ticket landing first. `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0` already exists and is public (lib/specled_ex/temp_name.ex:18) and is already used from a test (tracer_bootstrap_test.exs:20), so option 2 needs no new API and cannot move an api_boundary hash.

FLAKE NOTE: hash_store_test.exs is `async: true`; the option-2a change is strictly de-flaking. tracer_test.exs is `async: false` and mutates the shared `_build/<env>/.spec` manifest — do not run its edits concurrently with a compile of the same _build.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate (which is what you implement).

## Allowed touches
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names_reach.md` — BODY PROSE
  ONLY (Context / Decision / Consequences). Do NOT edit the `affects:`
  frontmatter list: widening it trips `specled.append_only.adr_affects_widened`.
- `test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs`
- `test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs`
- `.spec/specs/verification.spec.md` — spec co-change is AUTHORIZED, and takes
  precedence over Out of Scope, when the repo's spec gate demands it
  (missing-subject-update or realization-drift findings). Make the smallest edit
  that keeps `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` green.

## Out of Scope (files)
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names.md` — superseded; leave it alone.
- The other ~28 test files combining `System.tmp_dir!()` with `unique_integer`.
  Do NOT bulk-convert them; that is explicitly rejected by the mandate.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — the orchestrator consolidates the 0.11.0 section once at the
  end. Do not append.
- `VERSION` — the release step owns the bump.
- `.spec/realization_hashes.json` — no child in this epic may touch it. A hash
  diff is a red flag: stop and report it in your completion record; never
  regenerate it.
- `.spec/state.json` — derived, untracked, gitignored. Never commit.
- Every file not listed under Allowed touches.

## Out of Scope (intent)
- No new dependencies; `mix.exs` and `mix.lock` must be unchanged.
- No opportunistic refactors, renames, or drive-by tests outside the mandate.
- Do not weaken spec prose, and do not add a false `decisions:` link to
  `prose_guard.spec.md`, to quiet branch-guard. Use a `Spec-Drift:` commit
  trailer, as recent history on this repo already does.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/specled_ex/realization/hash_store_test.exs test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs`
3. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite. The
orchestrator owns whole-system proof at the merge gate and PR CI.

    Would fail if SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0 stopped emitting `<os-pid>_<12 hex>`
    or the verifier stopped using it — the `$0`-echoed script basename is matched against

Gaps:
- MERGE GATE BROKEN — `mix format --check-formatted` exits 1 on
  test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs. CLAUDE.md lists it as a required merge gate,
  and this commit introduced the violation: the base blob at 2023373d formats clean
  (verified by extracting `git show 2023373d:test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs`
  and running the formatter on it -> exit 0). Both edited hunks wrap `Enum.filter/2`
  across three lines where the formatter collapses to one:
    :384-386 and :420-422 ->
    `|> Enum.filter(&String.starts_with?(&1, "xref_mfa.etf.tmp.#{System.pid()}_"))`
  (~87 cols, inside the default line_length of 98; .formatter.exs sets no override).
  This is not a style preference — it is a deterministic gate failure that will stop the
  orchestrator's merge gate and PR CI. Fix is `mix format`. Note the SCOPE CONTRACT's
  three-command Verification list omits format, which is plausibly why it was missed;
  worth adding to the contract template.
- DELIVERABLE SELF-CONTRADICTION — ADR :59-64 vs. the same commit's tracer_test.exs fix.
  The new normative sentence reads: "That permission does **not** extend to tests that
  assert on directory contents (`File.ls!` over a shared or tmp root, **or a cleanup
  sweep that deletes by glob in a shared dir**). Those shall use
  `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0`."
  The repo contains exactly one member of that second class — tracer_test.exs:417-423
  (`File.rm(Path.join(Path.dirname(@manifest_path), &1))`, confirmed by sweeping
  `File.rm(Path.join` across test/: one hit). This commit changed that exact sweep, and
  it does NOT use cross_vm_suffix/0 — it filters on raw `System.pid()`.
  Worse, the prescription is *unsatisfiable* for that class, not merely unfollowed:
  cross_vm_suffix/0 mints fresh `:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(6)` on every call, so it can
  only NAME a path you allocate — it can never MATCH names a different writer produced.
  A reader who follows ADR :61 literally for a shared-dir sweep writes a filter containing
  a fresh random suffix, which matches nothing: `assert litter == []` becomes silently
  vacuous and the cleanup becomes a no-op. That is a worse outcome than the status quo,
  and it is precisely the "an unexplained sentence invites a reader to conclude something
  that is not true" failure this ticket was opened to remove — reintroduced one paragraph
  below the sentence it replaced.
  The ADR also never documents the remedy the commit actually shipped (pid-scoping the
  filter), so the durable decision does not describe its own implementation.
  Smallest fix — split the prescription by which half of the class you are in, e.g.:
    "Those shall scope by cross-VM identity: a test that ALLOCATES its own root shall
     name it with `SpecLedEx.TempName.cross_vm_suffix/0`; a test that sweeps a genuinely
     shared directory it cannot uniquify (e.g. `_build/<env>/.spec`) shall filter on the
     writer's `System.pid()` prefix instead, because a random suffix cannot match names
     another writer produced."
  This is one clause and stays inside the Allowed-touches prose region. In fairness to
  the implementer: the offending sentence was transcribed near-verbatim from the
  2026-07-27T08:37:06Z ADMISSION VERIFICATION mandate, which carries the same tension
  between its option-1 wording and its own option-2b pid-filtering instruction. The
  mandate is where the defect originates; it still ships in this deliverable.

Notes:
- Not a gap: narrowing the `litter` filter from `contains?(".tmp.")` to the pid-prefixed
  form is a real reduction in what that one assertion can catch, but the paired
  `atomic_tmp_name_includes_pid` test (:391-415, unchanged) independently pins the name
  shape, so no regression escapes both. The audit called this leg "optional"; taking it
  was the right call given the shared `_build/<env>/.spec` root.
- hash_store_test.exs:10 conversion is clean and does exactly what the mandate's option 2a
